name: Elderbridge Agency on Aging
description: Iowa’s six Area Agencies on Aging help adults 60 and older, people with disabilities and caregivers find help at home, meals, caregiver support, elder abuse prevention and options counseling.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. LifeLong Links, 866-468-7887, also connects callers to their Area Agency on Aging. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
Offices in Mason City, Carroll, Fort Dodge and Spencer.

name: Iowa Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
organization: Iowa Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
The same toll-free number reaches your local long-term care ombudsman.

source_evidence.title: Iowa HHS: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
source_evidence.scope: Toll-free 866-236-1430 for the state office and local ombudsmen; 321 E. 12th St., 2nd Floor, Des Moines; read in full. Last updated September 30, 2026. Local ombudsmen are shown only on a map image, so every county shows the toll-free line.
